notice: Feed-derived editorial examples. Each summary is an original paraphrase and must be reviewed before publication.

voices.name: Stuart Heritage
voices.quality_note: An active written feed with reviews, live episode coverage and television criticism. Only article metadata is imported; any short take remains editorial.

items.title: The Celebrity Traitors: episode one — as it happened
items.summary: Live written coverage of the opening episode and its unusually star-heavy cast.

items.title: The Guide #261: There is so much good telly this autumn you may never go outside again
items.summary: A broad autumn television survey designed as a route into several shows rather than one ranked recommendation.

voices.name: Peter Bradshaw
voices.quality_note: A high-frequency written UK film source whose review headlines usually identify one work cleanly.

items.title: Take It or Leave It
items.summary: Bradshaw responds to the film as an atmospheric account of Madness before fame.

items.title: Extra Geography
items.summary: He highlights its comedy and its treatment of class, sex and female friendship.

items.title: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
items.summary: Bradshaw presents the documentary as both frightening and life-affirming.

voices.name: Lucy Mangan
voices.quality_note: A named UK television critic with a dependable author feed and consistently title-specific reviews.

items.title: Kill Jackie
items.summary: Mangan finds the assassin thriller lacking in both character and plotting despite its familiar premise.

items.title: The Celebrity Traitors
items.summary: Her response centres on Ross Kemp’s conspicuous struggle to stay composed.

items.title: East of Eden
items.summary: Mangan praises Florence Pugh and finds the Steinbeck adaptation compelling television.

voices.name: Nick Creamer · Wrong Every Time
voices.quality_note: Long-form episode criticism and weekly viewing diaries arrive as complete written articles through a working RSS feed.

items.title: Summer 2026 — Week 13 in Review
items.summary: A weekly viewing diary covering current anime alongside feature films, kept as a collection rather than forced onto one title.

items.title: Apocalypse Hotel — Episode 6
items.summary: Close episode criticism focused on hospitality, inheritance and the series’ use of long-term hope.

items.title: The Mighty Nein — Episode 5
items.summary: An episode essay on adaptation choices, group failure and how tabletop play becomes coherent television drama.

voices.name: Alexis Petridis
voices.quality_note: A named UK music critic whose review headlines usually expose artist and release; quizzes, rankings and live reviews are filtered out.

items.title: Meshell Ndegeocello — Synonym
items.summary: Petridis admires the record’s vivid reinventions of songs from a deliberately wide range of writers.

items.title: Gilla Band — Pugnello
items.summary: He responds to the album’s aggression, absurd humour and refusal to sound ordinary.

items.title: Beabadoobee — Pylon
items.summary: Petridis finds recognisable feeling inside a louder record about rock-star frustration.
